Team / Anna — I reviewed the redline and annotated the attached PDF with line-by-line comments. Summary of suggested positions and proposed compromise language below. If the customer agrees, we can incorporate these into a fresh redline and proceed to DocuSign.

1) Subprocessor notices and objections
Proposal:
- Routine subprocessors: Redwood will provide written notice at least 30 days prior to engagement.
- Urgent security subprocessors (e.g., emergency patching, incident remediation): Redwood may engage with 5 days' prior notice and will notify the customer promptly; customer retains right to object within 15 days after notice — reasonable business grounds required.
- Redwood will publish an up-to-date list of subprocessors at https://www.redwoodinference.com/subprocessors and notify customers by email when material changes occur.

Rationale: 30 days is a common market compromise and balances customer review needs and operational agility. A short urgent notice carve-out avoids blocking critical security work.

2) Backup retention and deletion for customer-initiated deletions
Proposal:
- Primary deletion: Redwood will mark the customer's data for deletion within 5 business days of receiving an authenticated deletion request.
- Backup/archival copies: Redwood will remove customer data from backups and archival stores within 90 days; we will maintain limited backups for disaster recovery but will not use data for other purposes.
- For higher-assurance deletion (e.g., legal/regulatory requirements), Redwood will offer a certified deletion option subject to a scoped statement of work and associated fees.

Rationale: Operationally realistic while addressing customer expectations. We can shorten the backup window on case-by-case basis for enterprise customers with contractual commitments.

3) Cross-border transfers (SCCs + addendum)
Proposal:
- Redwood commits to execute the EU Commission SCCs (latest version) as the primary transfer mechanism.
- For customers that require an explicit EU addendum, Redwood will sign the Redwood EU Data Transfer Addendum (we have a template) provided downstream legal review is completed within 10 business days.
- We will implement reasonable technical measures (encryption at-rest/in-transit, access controls) and document them in our security datasheet.

Rationale: SCCs are widely accepted; offering a signable addendum where required avoids lengthy contract stalls.

4) Audit rights / SOC reports
Proposal:
- Redwood will provide annual SOC 2 Type II report and summarized penetration test results under NDA.
- Customer-specific on-site audits are permitted with 45 days' prior notice, limited to once per 12 months, and with reasonable confidentiality protections; costs borne by the customer unless Redwood's compliance materially fails.

5) Execution pathway
Recommendation:
- Incorporate the above language into a fresh redline and share with Clearline legal.
- If accepted, prepare DocuSign envelope to execute the DPA and follow up with a short mutual action plan documented in HubSpot (deal CL-2026-0911).

Attachment: Counsel_Annotated_DPA_v2.pdf (pdf)
